paragraphs.source_en: This habit didn’t come naturally to everyone. My older brother Stephen is the author of *The Speed of Trust* and a world-renowned speaker. He is always so prepared and never gives a speech without doing significant research on the organization he’s speaking to. But as a kid, he was the worst procrastinator of all time. The night before any big test or paper was due, he’d stay up all night working until the wee hours of the morning, and then he’d try to fit in an hour or two of sleep. He would literally lie on the kitchen table, with all of the lights on, knowing that somebody would inevitably run into him while making toast for breakfast. He could not risk sleeping through class, and there was no other way he’d be able to get up. This lifestyle finally caught up to him one day, however, when he had put off doing his math homework for the entire semester.

paragraphs.source_en: Learning to Put First Things First is hard. In fact, this is the habit, in general, that people struggle with most. This explains why my father felt compelled to write *First Things First* soon after completing *The 7 Habits*.
